newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone sees "pretty large" Centeon impact.
newsitem.headline: Rhone sees "pretty large" Centeon impact.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA expects a negative impact from the Centeon product recall in the 1997 results but good operating results at other units allow it to stick to a 20 percent profit rise target.

Jean-Pierre Titouflet, Rhone-Poulenc vice-president for financial affairs, told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday that the impact of Centeon would be "a pretty large one" but he gave no details.
Centeon LCC is a joint venture between Rhone's 68-percent owned Rhone-Poulenc Rorer and Germany's Hoechst. It recalled its blood plasma products in October.

Tirouflet said that at Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, synergy effects of the acquisition of Fisons were exceeding expectations. He noted that the anti-cancer drug Taxotere and the Tripedia vaccine were selling well.

Tirouflet said that the chemicals division, despite a drop in first-quarter earnings, was faring better than expected and he said a turnaround in prices in the titanium dioxide market were expected in the second half.
Rhone-Poulenc was on target to cut its debt-equity ratio to below 50 percent at the end of the year, he said. He did not give the first quarter figure.
